title: The 1-3-5 Method: How 1 pillar piece of content becomes 16
summary: Welsh explains his 1-3-5 content method: create one deep pillar piece, extract three core ideas, and turn each into five micro-pieces. It lets creators produce consistent, varied content across formats without burning out, since results matter more than hours spent.

principles.text: Creators are rewarded for results, not hours, so be efficient with content effort.
principles.quote: Because we aren’t rewarded by the hours we spend, we’re rewarded by the results we produce. So we have to be smart and efficient with our efforts.

principles.text: Start with one deep pillar piece on a big audience pain point; it makes all other content faster.
principles.quote: Creating this pillar piece of content will be the hardest part of the process. But it makes rest of the content production much faster and easier.

principles.text: Extract three standalone core ideas from the pillar piece.
principles.quote: Next, you want to extract three main concepts or tips from your pillar piece. These should be substantial enough to stand alone as valuable content.

principles.text: Turn each core idea into five micro pieces across formats: written posts, short video, carousel, poll.
principles.quote: Now, for **each** of your three core ideas, you’ll create five pieces of micro-content:

principles.text: Repurposing one deep piece across formats keeps your message consistent while adding variety.
principles.quote: You’re beating the same drum with some variety. This will naturally reinforce your brand and your message.

principles.text: Multiple formats meet audience members where they prefer to consume content.
principles.quote: The 1-3-5 method meets people where they consume best.
